request: how does 23 × 14 work as an area?

beats.intent: A 23 by 14 rectangle
beats.narration: Think of twenty three times fourteen as the area of a rectangle.
beats.code:
stage.title("23 × 14 as an area")
big = Rectangle(width=4.6, height=2.8, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(big))
stage.label(big, "23", direction=UP)
stage.label(big, "14", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: The rectangle split into four parts: 20×10, 3×10, 20×4, 3×4
beats.narration: Split twenty three into twenty and three, and fourteen into ten and four: four smaller rectangles.
beats.code:
a = Rectangle(width=4, height=2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(big.get_corner(UL) + np.array([2, -1, 0]))
b = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(a, RIGHT, buff=0)
c = Rectangle(width=4, height=0.8, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(a, DOWN, buff=0)
d = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.8, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(c, RIGHT, buff=0)
stage.play(FadeIn(a), FadeIn(b), FadeIn(c), FadeIn(d))
stage.add(a, b, c, d)
for r, t in ((a, "200"), (b, "30"), (c, "80"), (d, "12")):
    stage.play(FadeIn(Text(t, font_size=24).move_to(r)))

beats.intent: The four parts beside 200 + 30 + 80 + 12 = 322
beats.narration: Add the four areas: two hundred, thirty, eighty and twelve make three hundred and twenty two.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"200 + 30 + 80 + 12 = 322")

request: why is a tangent to a circle at right angles to the radius?

beats.intent: A circle with its centre and a radius to a point P
beats.narration: Draw a circle, its centre, and a radius out to a point P.
beats.code:
stage.title("Tangent and radius")
c = draw_circle(stage, radius=2)
O = c.get_center()
P = O + 2 * np.array([np.cos(PI / 4), np.sin(PI / 4), 0])
rad = Line(O, P, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(rad), FadeIn(Dot(O)), FadeIn(Dot(P, color=RED)))
stage.add(rad)

beats.intent: The tangent line at P touching the circle once
beats.narration: The tangent at P touches the circle at that one point and nowhere else.
beats.code:
dirn = np.array([-np.sin(PI / 4), np.cos(PI / 4), 0])
tan = Line(P - 2.2 * dirn, P + 2.2 * dirn, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(tan))
stage.add(tan)

beats.intent: The right-angle mark between radius and tangent at P
beats.narration: They meet at exactly ninety degrees: any other line through P would cut back into the circle.
beats.code:
ra = RightAngle(Line(P, O), Line(P, P + dirn), length=0.3, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(ra))
stage.add(ra)
stage.caption("Radius and tangent meet at 90°")

beats.intent: A single regular hexagon
beats.narration: A bee wants cells that cover the comb with no gaps.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why hexagons?")
hexa = lambda c: RegularPolygon(6, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.4).scale(0.6).move_to(c)
h0 = hexa(ORIGIN)
stage.play(Create(h0))

beats.intent: Hexagons tiling the plane with no gaps
beats.narration: Hexagons fit together perfectly, edge to edge, with nothing left over.
beats.code:
cells = VGroup(*[hexa(np.array([1.04 * (i + 0.5 * (j % 2)), 0.9 * j, 0])) for i in range(-3, 3) for j in range(-2, 3)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(h) for h in cells], lag_ratio=0.03), run_time=2)
stage.add(cells)

beats.intent: Bars comparing perimeter for equal area: triangle 4.6, square 4.0, hexagon 3.7
beats.narration: Of the shapes that tile, the hexagon encloses the same area with the least wall: the least wax.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [4.56, 4.0, 3.72], labels=["triangle", "square", "hexagon"])
highlight(stage, bars[2])
stage.caption("Least wall for the same area")

request: why does the moon have phases?

beats.intent: The sun's light coming from the left onto the Earth and the moon in orbit
beats.narration: Sunlight comes from one side. The moon circles the Earth.
beats.code:
stage.title("Phases of the moon")
earth = Circle(radius=0.4, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.9)
orbit = DashedVMobject(Circle(radius=2.2, color=GREY), num_dashes=40)
rays = VGroup(*[Arrow(np.array([-6.5, y, 0]), np.array([-5, y, 0]), buff=0, color=YELLOW) for y in (-1.5, 0, 1.5)])
stage.play(FadeIn(earth), Create(orbit), FadeIn(rays))
stage.add(earth, orbit, rays)

beats.intent: Four moons around the orbit, each lit on its sunward half
beats.narration: The moon's sunward half is always lit, wherever it is.
beats.code:
def moon(angle):
    c = 2.2 * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
    dark = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(c)
    lit = AnnularSector(inner_radius=0, outer_radius=0.3, angle=PI, start_angle=PI / 2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_arc_center_to(c)
    return VGroup(dark, lit)
moons = VGroup(*[moon(a) for a in (0, PI / 2, PI, 3 * PI / 2)])
stage.play(FadeIn(moons))
stage.add(moons)

beats.intent: The moon at the far side labelled full and at the sun's side labelled new
beats.narration: From Earth, when the moon is on the far side we see all of its lit half: full. On the sun's side we see only the dark half: new.
beats.code:
stage.label(moons[0], "full (seen from Earth)", direction=RIGHT)
stage.label(moons[2], "new", direction=LEFT)
stage.caption("How much lit half faces us")

request: what does simple harmonic motion look like on a graph?

beats.intent: Axes of time against displacement with a dot tracing x = cos t
beats.narration: A mass on a spring moves back and forth; its position over time traces a cosine.
beats.code:
stage.title("A mass on a spring")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 12.6), y_range=(-1.5, 1.5), labels=("t", "x"))
trace_graph(stage, ax, np.cos, 0, 12.6)

beats.intent: The peaks marked at t = 0, 2π, 4π, one period of 2π apart
beats.narration: It returns to the same place every two pi seconds: the period.
beats.code:
for t in (0, TAU, 2 * TAU):
    mark_point(stage, ax, t, 1, color=RED)
br = Brace(Line(ax.c2p(0, 1.2), ax.c2p(TAU, 1.2)), UP)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(br))
stage.label(br, "period 2π", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: The velocity curve -sin t added in green, zero where the position peaks
beats.narration: Its speed is greatest in the middle and zero at the ends, where it turns round.
beats.code:
v = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: -np.sin(t), color=GREEN, label="velocity")
stage.caption("Fastest in the middle, still at the ends")

request: how do you find the area of a triangle from its corners?

beats.intent: A grid with the triangle (0, 0), (4, 0), (1, 3)
beats.narration: A triangle with corners at zero, zero; four, zero; and one, three.
beats.code:
stage.title("Area from coordinates")
p = draw_plane(stage, x_extent=5, y_extent=4)
tri = Polygon(p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(4, 0), p.c2p(1, 3), color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.4)
stage.play(Create(tri))
stage.add(tri)

beats.intent: The base 4 along the x-axis and the height 3 drawn as a dashed line
beats.narration: Its base along the x axis is four, and its height is three.
beats.code:
h = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(1, 0), p.c2p(1, 3), color=RED, dashed=True)
stage.label(h, "3", direction=LEFT, color=RED)
base = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(4, 0), color=GREEN)
stage.label(base, "4", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The triangle beside Area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6
beats.narration: Half of base times height: six square units.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\text{Area} = \tfrac12 \times 4 \times 3 = 6")

request: what's the difference between speed and velocity?

beats.intent: A circular track with a runner dot and a velocity arrow along the track
beats.narration: A runner goes round a circular track at a steady five metres per second.
beats.code:
stage.title("Speed vs velocity")
track = draw_circle(stage, radius=2)
c = track.get_center()
at = lambda a: c + 2 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0])
tang = lambda a: np.array([-np.sin(a), np.cos(a), 0])
runner = Dot(at(0), color=YELLOW, radius=0.12)
arr = Arrow(at(0), at(0) + 1.2 * tang(0), buff=0, color=GREEN)
stage.play(FadeIn(runner), GrowArrow(arr))
stage.add(runner, arr)

beats.intent: The runner a quarter lap on, the arrow the same length but pointing a new way
beats.narration: A quarter lap later the arrow is just as long, same speed, but points a different way: a different velocity.
beats.code:
stage.play(Rotate(VGroup(runner, arr), PI / 2, about_point=c), run_time=1.5)
stage.caption("Same speed, new direction")

beats.intent: Both arrows side by side with speed = 5 m/s and velocity as an arrow
beats.narration: Speed is just how fast. Velocity is how fast and which way.
beats.code:
ghost = Arrow(at(0), at(0) + 1.2 * tang(0), buff=0, color=GREEN).set_opacity(0.35)
stage.play(FadeIn(ghost))
stage.add(ghost)
stage.equation(r"|\vec v| = 5\ \text{m/s both times}")

request: how can a small sample tell you about a whole population?

beats.intent: A grid of 100 dots, 30 of them red
beats.narration: A town of a hundred people, thirty of whom like a new park.
beats.code:
stage.title("Sampling")
dots = draw_dots(stage, n=100, cols=20)
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
liked = set(rng.choice(100, 30, replace=False).tolist())
stage.play(*[dots[k].animate.set_color(RED) for k in liked])

beats.intent: Ten dots picked at random and circled, the red ones among them counted
beats.narration: Ask ten people picked at random and count how many like it.
beats.code:
pick = [k for k in rng.choice(100, 10, replace=False).tolist()]
rings = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.16, color=WHITE).move_to(dots[k]) for k in pick])
stage.play(Create(rings))
stage.add(rings)
stage.caption(f"{sum(k in liked for k in pick)} of 10 sampled like it")

beats.intent: Bars comparing the sample's share to the true 30%
beats.narration: The sample's share is a good guess at the whole town's thirty percent, and bigger samples guess better.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
share = sum(k in liked for k in pick) / 10
bars = draw_bars(stage, [share, 0.3], labels=["sample", "town"])
